name: generate_plugin_scaffold
description: Generate (or regenerate) a complete local plugin on disk: profile.json, plugin.py (the udi_interface Controller, with wiring methods always tool-generated and override-method bodies supplied here), any extra node-class files, main.py, version.py, server_entry.json (the exact local-install registration payload), README.md, tests, and an append-only context.md iteration note. Refuses if no evidence has been gathered this session (call search_store_plugins/search_github_plugins/search_web/fetch_reference first), if the profile fails validate_profile's checks, if override_bodies names an unknown method, or if anything generated appears to contain a real secret value -- OAuth client_id/client_secret are always written as a fixed placeholder, filled in for real after install via configure_plugin(key='oauth'). If any target file already exists, the first call returns the conflict list and writes nothing; call again with confirm_overwrite: true once the customer has agreed to overwrite. Follow with install_generated_plugin to actually register/install/start it.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root to write this plugin into. Reuse the 'location' from list_generated_plugins/read_generated_plugin when updating an existing plugin.

profile.description: The Dynamic Profiles wire document -- top-level 'editors'/'nodedefs'/'linkdefs' lists, the same shape polyglot.getJsonProfile()/read_generated_plugin use. Internally wrapped and checked with the same structural validation validate_profile runs before anything is written.

controller_class.description: The Controller class name to generate in plugin.py. Defaults to 'Controller'.

controller_module.description: The module (filename without .py) main.py imports the controller class from. Defaults to 'plugin'.

version.description: The plugin version string written to version.py and passed to polyglot.start(). Defaults to '1.0.0'; bump on every regeneration that changes behavior.

node_classes.description: Extra device Node subclasses beyond the Controller, as {filename_without_py: full_python_source}, for profiles with more than one NodeDef.

override_bodies.description: Full Python method source (the 'def ...():' line through its body, properly indented as a class method) for each override this plugin needs, keyed by method name: start, stop, discover, shortPoll, longPoll, processConfig, parameterHandler, customParamHandler -- plus handle_custom_request and one '_<tool_name>' helper per server_entry.aiTools entry when server_entry.ai_enabled is true. Any name not supplied gets a safe no-op stub. Any other key is rejected.

server_entry.description: The developer/tool-defined registration spec -- becomes server_entry.json, the exact PUT /api/plugins/store/local/entry body install_generated_plugin sends.

runAs.description: OS account the plugin process runs as. Defaults to 'eisyai'.

customParams.description: The developer-defined custom-config schema (field names/descriptions/types) -- NOT real values. Real values are filled in afterward by the customer via configure_plugin.

authorize.description: True if this plugin needs OAuth against the target API.

oauth.description: OAuth endpoint config when authorize is true: auth_endpoint, token_endpoint, scope, addRedirect, addScope, token_parameters. Never include a real client_id/client_secret -- omit them and the placeholder is filled in automatically.

ai_enabled.description: True only if this plugin exposes AI-callable tools via CUSTOMREQUEST.

aiPrompt.description: Static developer-authored prompt text describing this plugin's AI tools.

aiTools.description: Each declared AI tool: {name, description, params?}. Every entry needs a matching '_<name>' helper in override_bodies.

devd.description: Only for plugins needing direct serial/USB hardware access. {vendor_id, product_id, name} (vendor_id/product_id as 4-hex-digit strings, e.g. from detect_usb_device) renders the devd.conf hardware-attach rule text. Omit entirely for API/cloud-service-backed plugins (the common case).

readme_body.description: The README's main body text. A 'Sources' section citing every evidence source gathered this session is appended automatically.

tests.description: Generated test files, as {filename: python_source} (filenames should start with 'test_').

iteration_note.description: A short note on what this generation call changed -- appended to context.md so a later session (or read_generated_plugin) can see the plugin's iteration history.

confirm_overwrite.description: Set true only after the customer has explicitly agreed to overwrite an existing plugin's files (the first call without this returns the conflict list and writes nothing).
